title: Estimate video streaming bandwidth
scenario: A video platform wants to know how much bandwidth it needs and whether a CDN is worth it. Viewers watch at **5 Mbit/s** on average. Use decimal units (1 Gbit = 1,000 Mbit, 1 TB = 1,000,000 MB) and 86,400 seconds per day. Anything within 25% counts.

givens.label: Minutes watched per viewer per day
Share of traffic served by the CDN

questions.prompt: Average number of people watching at the same moment
Peak egress bandwidth, before the CDN
Peak egress that still reaches the origin servers with the CDN

solution:
1. **Concurrent viewers (Little's law):** watch time per day is 5 million × 40 minutes = 200 million minutes = 12 billion seconds. Spread over 86,400 seconds, that's 12,000,000,000 ÷ 86,400 ≈ **139,000 people watching at any moment** on average.
2. **Peak egress:** 139,000 × 5 Mbit/s ≈ 694,000 Mbit/s ≈ 694 Gbit/s on average, × 3 at peak ≈ **2,100 Gbit/s** (about 2 Tbit/s). No single data center serves that comfortably.
3. **Origin egress with a CDN:** the CDN absorbs 95%, so 5% of 2,083 Gbit/s ≈ **104 Gbit/s** reaches the origin. The CDN turns an impossible number into a large but manageable one.
4. **Daily volume:** 12 billion seconds × 5 Mbit/s = 60 billion Mbit = 60,000,000,000 ÷ 8 MB ≈ 7.5 billion MB = **7,500 TB (7.5 PB) per day**. At this scale, CDN pricing and caching efficiency dominate the cost of running the service.
